npcs.name: Tullia Vesk
npcs.greet: Mind the ink, it is still wet. I have been copying Ayleid lamp-glyphs since dawn and my hand has forgotten how to stop.

npcs.name: Pia Lucanus
npcs.greet: If you've come for a burial, the shop is shut. Master Valcis has not come home in nine days, and I cannot lift the coffins alone.

npcs.name: Septima Merula
npcs.greet: I keep the graves of men who have no graves. It is quieter work than it sounds, until someone asks me why.

npcs.name: Lady Cassia Vallarius
npcs.greet: You may bow, or not. My grandfather would have had you whipped for the omission. I am trying very hard not to be my grandfather.

npcs.name: Aldo Castellus
npcs.greet: Castellus red. Forty years in the cask, and the best thing you will ever taste. Assuming the Merovanes leave me a single vine to make it with.

npcs.name: Ysmene Merovane
npcs.greet: Merovane tawny, my friend. Sweeter than Castellus and twice as honest. If old Aldo sent you, you may leave the way you came.

npcs.name: Inspector Marcellin Hesk
npcs.greet: Harbor customs. Everything that comes into Anvil passes my desk, and everything that leaves it without passing my desk is my problem.

npcs.name: Sabine
npcs.greet: Keep your hands where the lantern can see them. Nobody comes to Hrota Cave for the view.

npcs.name: Drevis Hlaren
npcs.greet: Captain of the Cheydinhal watch. Speak plainly, outlander. Three merchants are dead and I am out of patience for riddles.

npcs.name: Seeks-the-Shallows
npcs.greet: My boat goes where the water goes. If you want somewhere the water does not go, find a horse.

npcs.name: Little-Reed
npcs.greet: The singing stopped. Is it safe to stop holding my breath now?

npcs.name: Hrefna Cold-Harp
npcs.greet: Every song in Bruma is about snow. I mean to write one about something that bites back.

npcs.name: Tullo Brash
npcs.greet: Lend a coin, borrow a coin, it's all the same to Tullo. Unless you're late paying it back.

npcs.name: Pellio Brash
npcs.greet: Put the sword down. I'm not who you think I am. Well. I am, but not the way you've been told.

npcs.name: Feldsa Sadrathi
npcs.greet: Forgive the mess, sera. Our family shrine was robbed, and a house without its ancestors is only a pile of furniture.

npcs.name: Ervyn Sadrathi
npcs.greet: Did my mother send you? Whatever she said, I was nowhere near the shrine. I was at the tavern. Ask anyone. Ask the tavern.

relics.name: The Undimmed Lamp
relics.desc: A welkynd lantern no bigger than a fist. The light inside it does not flicker, and it does not feel friendly.

relics.name: Starved Welkynd Stone
relics.desc: A blue Ayleid stone, nearly dark. It warms slightly when held under the open sky at night.

relics.name: Istirus Duty Roll
relics.desc: The fort's last roll of the watch, in the prefect's own hand. One name is marked absent, and it is his.

relics.name: Aurelian Vallarius' Household Book
relics.desc: Accounts, births and deaths of House Vallarius. A page near the back has been cut out with a very sharp knife.

relics.name: Livia's Black Feather
relics.desc: A long hagraven quill tied with a faded Vallarius ribbon in green and gold.

relics.name: Blighted Vine-Root
relics.desc: A grape root wrapped in pale threads, like hair. It smells of wet earth and something sweeter.

relics.name: Vine-Wife's Heartseed
relics.desc: A seed the size of a plum, green and faintly warm, with a pulse you can feel if you hold still.

relics.name: Salt-Stained Ledger
relics.desc: A smuggler's book of cargo: welkynd stones by the crate, paid for in Summerset gold. Some payments go to the Anvil customs house.

relics.name: Thrice-Turned Dagger
relics.desc: A plain iron dagger with a hilt wrapped in grey silk. The blade has been bent three times and straightened three times.

relics.name: Letter of the Ninth Turn
relics.desc: Unsigned, sealed in grey wax. It speaks of 'the stranger who kills for us' as though it were a blessing.

relics.name: Rimeoath
relics.desc: An old Nord sword rimed with frost that never melts. Runes along the fuller name a promise, not an owner.

relics.name: Sadrathi Ash-Urn
relics.desc: A small urn of red Morrowind clay, sealed with wax. It is heavier than ash should be, and it occasionally sighs.

relics.name: Valcis' Ledger of Remains
relics.desc: An undertaker's book of names and prices. Most entries end in 'buried'. Some end in 'sold'.

side_cyr_narindel_whispers: The air in Narindel tastes of old lamp-oil. Somewhere below, a blue light pulses slowly, like a sleeper's breath.
Another little Imperial with a lantern of her own. Come down, then. Every lamp in this place was lit with someone like you.
side_cyr_lamp_lifted: The moment the lamp leaves its niche, every welkynd in the hall goes dark at once.
Thief. I kept that flame for four thousand years. You will not keep it for four minutes.
side_cyr_well_wakes: The starved stone hums. Far down the dry well, something answers in a voice like glass being drawn across glass.
Two wells, and the door. Light them for me, walker, and I will show you a star that fell and did not break.
side_cyr_anyandil_door: The sealed door of Anyandil slides apart at the touch of the brightened stone. Beyond it, a lump of black meteoric glass sits on a dais, and it is breathing.
You lit the wells. You opened the door. You were very kind. I have not stretched my wings in nine hundred years.
side_cyr_istirus_roll_call: At midnight, pale shapes in Legion red form two ranks in the yard of Fort Istirus. Their necks are bent at the same wrong angle.
Roll of the watch! Twenty men present. Deserters, every one, and hanged for it. Again, from the top.
No ghost answers to the twenty-first name. The prefect never calls it.
side_cyr_rayles_roost: Feathers and bones hang from the broken gate of Fort Rayles, tied with ribbons of green and gold.
Gold and green. Do you know those colours, little errand-runner? I wore them once, before my brother cut me out of the book.
Every heir of Vallarius sickens at thirty because every heir of Vallarius forgets me. Tell Cassia that, if you live.
side_cyr_grove_speaks: Moonlight on the ruin of Talwinque. Among the stumps of an old grove, a woman made of bark and grapevine rises from the ground.
Two young men with one axe between them. Castellus and Merovane. They cut my grove to plant their first rows, and shook hands over the stumps.
Thirty summers I waited. Now their vines drink my sorrow, and they blame each other. Let them. I am not finished.
side_cyr_hrota_meeting: The smugglers' leader lowers her crossbow. She has the inspector's jaw and the inspector's habit of squinting at strangers.
So my father sent you. Of course he did. Ask him where the Saltworks crew get their papers stamped, and watch his face.
side_cyr_naso_shrine: Inside Fort Naso, a statue of a hooded figure has been carved from a single block of grey stone. Every one of its hands holds a knife pointed at the one beside it.
Votive daggers lie at its feet, each bent and straightened three times.
side_cyr_boethiah_speaks: Snow hisses where it touches the shrine. The cultists part, and a Dunmer woman in grey steps forward, smiling.
The stranger who kills for us. Drevis promised you would come. He sent you to cut down Thalyn so he could climb, and now he hopes you will cut me down too.
A knife that knows whose hand it is in. How rare. Show me whether it can also choose.
side_cyr_drowned_rest_song: The stilt-houses of Drowned Rest are freshly painted and the people are very friendly. They sing to the water every evening, softly, like a lullaby.
No one here will say where the children are.
side_cyr_skeldhaugr_waking: Thieves in my hall. Do you not hear the ice groaning? I hold it shut. I have always held it shut. Put. It. Back.
side_cyr_oath_breaks: A crack like a falling tree echoes across the mountains. Snow slides from every ledge above the barrow.
Far up the slope, on the Giant's Stair, something very large stands up and stretches for the first time in an age.
side_cyr_lantern_follows: Past midnight, a single green lantern drifts along the far bank of the Larsius, too slow for a boat and too steady for a drunk.
It stops, as if waiting for you, and then sets off north.
side_cyr_valcis_ledger_read: Most of the names in the undertaker's book end with a burial fee. Too many end with a second price, larger, beside the word 'sold'.
Pia? Is that you, girl? Go home. The dead don't mind being useful, and neither should you.
side_cyr_wendir_bearer: A knight sits on a broken Ayleid step at Wendir with a black sword across his knees. He has not eaten in a long time. The sword has.
Another one. Good. This one is very tired. You look rested.
side_cyr_oxhorn_meets: A minotaur kneels beside a moss-covered cairn, scraping old Cyrodilic letters back into the stone with one horn.
Not a beast. A watchman. The Saint sleeps here, and I keep her sleep. The baron's dogs have found us. Will you stand, or run like the last one?
side_cyr_urn_speaks: The wax seal on the urn cracks the moment the necromancer falls. A thin grey shape coils up out of it, wearing a very disappointed expression.
Finally, someone competent. Do you know who carried me out of the shrine and sold me to that woman for forty drakes? My grandson. Forty! I was worth at least a hundred.
Ervyn said I talked too much. I am dead, outlander. Talking is all I have left.

quests.title: The Undimmed Lamp
quests.pitch: Lamp-glyphs from Narindel, an Ayleid ruin north of the Rumare that nobody bothers to rob anymore. The glyphs say the lamp in its lowest hall has never gone out, not once in four thousand years. I want to see it. I would very much like you to walk in front of me.
quests.desc: Tullia Vesk, a scholar in the Imperial City, asked me to find a welkynd lamp in the forgotten Ayleid ruin of Narindel, a lamp her glyphs say has never gone out.

objectives.text: Find the ruin of Narindel
Destroy the lamp-keepers of Narindel
Take the Undimmed Lamp from its niche
Destroy Herdaril the Undimmed
objectives.journal: The lich came apart like a snuffed wick. But the lamp in my pack was still burning, and it was warm against my back the whole way home.

objectives.text: Bring the lamp to Tullia Vesk
objectives.topic: The lamp kept a lich alive. It is still lit.
objectives.reply: Of course it is. It is not a lamp, it is a vessel. Herdaril poured himself into it. With the right glyphs, anyone could. Give it to me. Please.

choices.label: Here. Study it, and be careful.
choices.reply: Careful. Yes. I will be very careful. Thank you, truly. I will remember who helped me, for a very long time.

choices.label: No. I'm breaking it here, in front of you.
choices.reply: Don't... Oh. Oh, it's just glass now. You have no idea what you've thrown away. Get out. No, wait. Thank you. I think.

quests.outro: I brought the Undimmed Lamp out of Narindel and decided what became of it. Tullia Vesk will not soon forget that choice, whichever way it went.

quests.title: Wells of the Fallen Star

find.text: A standing stone carved with five Ayleid star-marks, four of them chipped dark. Beneath, in fresh charcoal: 'Under stars only. Dusk, then Morrow, then the door.' A dull blue stone sits in a hollow at its foot.

quests.desc: I found a carved stone in the Heartlands with a starved welkynd stone at its foot and directions to two Ayleid wells and a door.

objectives.text: Hold the welkynd stone over the Well of Dusk at night
objectives.journal: The stone drank the starlight over the Well of Dusk and something down in the dark said thank you.

objectives.text: Find the Well of Morrow to the south
Keep a vigil at the Well of Morrow while the stone brightens
objectives.journal: By the second hour the stone was too bright to look at. The well beside me had begun to hum.

objectives.text: Bring the brightened stone to the sealed door of Anyandil
Fight off the waking wardens of Anyandil
Break Ilvanor of the Fallen Star before it escapes
objectives.journal: The voice in the wells had never been a ghost asking for help. It was a prisoner asking for a key, and I had carried it all the way to the door.

quests.outro: Ilvanor shattered into black glass on the floor of Anyandil. Among the shards was a sliver of welkynd that still held the light of the wells.

quests.title: The Roll of Istirus

find.text: A plain headstone, far newer than the fort. Twenty names are cut into it, each scratched out and recut more deeply. At the bottom: 'They did not run. - S.M., Kvatch.'

quests.desc: Outside Fort Istirus I found a headstone for twenty legionaries, recut by someone in Kvatch who swears they did not desert.

objectives.text: Return to Fort Istirus after dark
Put down the hanged legionaries who still answer the roll
Search the prefect's quarters for the last duty roll
Face the shade of Prefect Vibius Aurex
objectives.journal: The prefect's shade fought hardest for the roll. It was his own handwriting that damned him: the night the fort was abandoned, the only man absent was the prefect.

objectives.text: Bring the roll to S.M. in Kvatch
objectives.topic: You recut the stone at Fort Istirus. This is the last roll of the watch.
objectives.reply: Septima Merula. My great-grandfather was the eleventh name. Let me read it. ...He ran. The prefect ran, and wrote them up as deserters to cover it. My family has been right for eighty years, and nobody listened.

objectives.text: Decide with Septima what to do with the truth
objectives.topic: What will you do with it?
objectives.reply: The Aurex family still sits on the Kvatch council. I could nail this to the chapel door. Or I could bury it with the men, and let them rest without a scandal. Which would you do?

choices.label: Nail it to the chapel door.
choices.reply: Then the whole Gold Coast will know their names were clean. The Aurexes will hate us both. Good.

choices.label: Bury it with them. They wanted rest, not revenge.
choices.reply: Maybe you're right. I'll take it to the fort myself and read the names one last time. Properly, this time.

quests.outro: The twenty hanged men of Fort Istirus no longer answer the roll. Septima Merula has the truth now, and the Aurex name will carry what it deserves, one way or another.

quests.title: Green and Gold
quests.pitch: Every heir of House Vallarius falls ill in their thirtieth year and is dead by the thirty-first. I turn thirty next month. My grandfather's household book was buried with him in our crypt in the hills west of here. If there is a reason for this, it is written there. Fetch it, and I will pay whatever you ask.
quests.desc: Lady Cassia Vallarius of Chorrol says every heir of her family dies at thirty. She sent me to the family crypt for her grandfather's household book.

objectives.text: Find the Vallarius crypt in the western hills
Recover the household book from Aurelian Vallarius' tomb
objectives.journal: A page was cut from the household book. On the next page, in the same hand: 'Livia is not to be spoken of. Payments to the witch at Rayles to continue.'

objectives.text: Follow the payments to Fort Rayles
Clear the hagraven's servants from Fort Rayles
Confront Mother Livia
objectives.journal: Livia Vallarius died cursing a family that had paid her to stay away for two hundred years. Her feather still had the family ribbon tied to it.

objectives.text: Tell Lady Cassia what was cut out of her family
objectives.topic: The curse had a name. Livia Vallarius.
objectives.reply: A great-great-aunt nobody remembers, struck from the book and paid to rot in a ruin. And every heir since kept paying, and kept forgetting why.

objectives.text: Help Cassia decide what the family book will say
objectives.topic: What will you write in the book?
objectives.reply: I could leave the page cut. Or I could write her back in, and let all of Chorrol read what we did.

choices.label: Write her back in. Names were the curse.
choices.reply: Then she goes back on the page, between her brother and her sister, where she should have been. I feel better already. That may only be pride.

choices.label: Leave it cut. Some debts are better buried.
choices.reply: You may be right. The Vallarius name has enough stains. I'll burn the feather and say nothing. My grandfather would approve, and that worries me.

quests.outro: The hagraven of Fort Rayles is dead and Lady Cassia Vallarius may live past thirty. What the family book says about Livia is now Cassia's to answer for.

quests.title: Blood on the Vine
quests.pitch: Rot. White rot, like hair, all through the roots. Started the week the Merovane woman bought her new press. Coincidence? I'm sixty-one, friend, I stopped believing in coincidence before you were born. Go and look at my rows. Then go and look at her face.
quests.desc: Aldo Castellus, a Skingrad vintner, says the Merovane family poisoned his vines. He wants proof.

objectives.text: Dig up a blighted root in the Castellus rows
Question Ysmene Merovane
objectives.topic: Aldo Castellus says you poisoned his vines.
objectives.reply: Then why are mine rotting too? Same pale threads, same smell. I assumed Aldo did it to me first. Look at the old stump grove near Talwinque if you want something strange. Nothing grows right in those hills, and nobody will say why.

objectives.text: Visit the stump grove at Talwinque by night
Fight off the grove's thorn-children
Defeat the Vine-Wife
objectives.journal: When the Vine-Wife fell, a warm green seed rolled out of the bark at her heart. It was still beating.

objectives.text: Plant the heartseed among the old stumps
objectives.journal: I planted the heartseed where the grove used to stand. By the time I stood up, a green shoot had already broken the soil.

objectives.text: Tell Aldo Castellus who really blighted the vines
objectives.topic: You and old Merovane cut down a spriggan's grove together, thirty years ago.
objectives.reply: ...Ennio Merovane and I. We were partners then, before the quarrel. Two boys with one axe. Gods. We have been blaming each other for our own sin.

choices.label: Tell Ysmene. End the feud.
choices.reply: She'll laugh at me. Then maybe she'll pour me a cup of that sweet tawny I pretend to hate. Fine. Fine! I'll go now, before I lose my nerve.

choices.label: Keep it quiet. Just pay me.
choices.reply: Easier, yes. Coward's choice, but easier. Here, take this, and a case of the forty-year. Don't drink it all on the road.

quests.outro: The blight in the West Weald came from a grove two young vintners cut down together. The Vine-Wife is gone, a new grove is growing, and Skingrad's feud is now in the hands of two stubborn families.

quests.title: Salt and Starlight
quests.pitch: Welkynd stones are leaving the Gold Coast by the crate, dug out of Ayleid ruins and sold to Summerset buyers. The crew doing it uses Hrota Cave, north of the city, at night. Clear them out and bring me their leader's books. The Empire pays well for its own history.
quests.desc: Inspector Marcellin Hesk of the Anvil customs house asked me to break a crew smuggling welkynd stones out of Hrota Cave.

objectives.text: Go to Hrota Cave after dark
Fight past the smugglers' lookouts
Hear out the smugglers' leader
objectives.topic: You're Hesk's daughter.
objectives.reply: Sabine. I run stones, yes. So does the Saltworks crew, twice as many, and their crates go out stamped by the customs house. Father isn't stopping smugglers. He's stopping competition.

choices.label: Then let's sink the Saltworks crew together.
choices.reply: Now you're thinking like a Hesk. Corvo Lask holds the Old Saltworks to the north. Bring me his ledger and we'll see whose name is in it.

choices.label: I don't care. You're coming back to Anvil.
choices.reply: Then you'll have to drag me, and my people will have something to say about that. Go deal with Lask first. If you live, we'll talk.

objectives.text: Survive the ambush on the coast road
Kill Corvo Lask, the Salt King
Take Lask's ledger
objectives.journal: Lask's ledger lists a payment to the Anvil customs house for every crate. The initials beside each one are M.H.

objectives.text: Confront Inspector Hesk with the ledger
objectives.topic: Lask paid you for every crate. And the other crew is your daughter's.
objectives.reply: ...She told you. Of course she did. Fine. Burn the book and keep my pay, and I'll retire quietly to a farm near Kvatch. Or take it to the Count and watch both Hesks hang. Your hand, your choice.

quests.outro: I broke the Saltworks crew and learned that the Anvil customs house had been taking its cut. Father and daughter Hesk have both been squinting at me ever since.

quests.title: The Thrice-Turned Knife
quests.pitch: A dagger. Turned three times in the wound, every time. Three merchants, three daggers, and not a coin stolen. That is not robbery, it is ritual. Find whoever is doing this, outlander, and I will owe you more than wages.
quests.desc: Captain Drevis Hlaren of the Cheydinhal watch asked me to find who is killing the city's merchants with daggers turned three times in the wound.

objectives.text: Search the last victim's house by the river
objectives.journal: The murder weapon was wrapped in grey silk. A Dunmer neighbor went pale when she saw it, and whispered one name: Boethiah.

objectives.text: Survive the knives sent to stop you
Follow the grey silk to Fort Naso
Break the cult cell in Fort Naso
Kill Thalyn Orvas, the Smiling Knife
objectives.journal: Thalyn Orvas died smiling. His last words were: 'Well turned, stranger. Tell him he climbed well.'

objectives.text: Search Thalyn's altar for orders
Bring the letter to Captain Hlaren
objectives.topic: The cell is broken. This letter was on their altar.
objectives.reply: The Ninth Turn, at the shrine in the Jerall. So there is a mother to this nest. Well done. Rest, outlander. I will send for you when I know more.

quests.outro: I broke a Boethiah cult cell in Fort Naso and brought Captain Hlaren a letter pointing to a shrine in the Jerall Mountains. Thalyn Orvas' last words keep coming back to me.

quests.title: The Ninth Turn
quests.desc: A courier from Captain Hlaren found me: the cult of the Thrice-Turned Knife gathers at Boethiah's shrine in the Jerall Mountains. Hlaren wants its High Blade dead.

objectives.text: Climb to Boethiah's shrine in the Jerall Mountains
Cut through the Turned Knives at the shrine
Kill Mother Sethra Vael, High Blade of the Turned Knife
objectives.journal: Sethra Vael told the truth before she died: Drevis Hlaren is one of them. Every blade I broke for him was a rival on his way to the top.

objectives.text: Face Captain Drevis Hlaren in Cheydinhal
objectives.topic: Sethra is dead. She told me whose knife I've been.
objectives.reply: Then you understand the Prince better than most priests. I am High Blade now, thanks to you. Join me, and the next turn is yours. Or turn on me. Either way, Boethiah will be pleased.

choices.label: I'm taking this to the Count of Cheydinhal.
choices.reply: Of course you are. The faithful betray, and betrayal is faith. I will be gone before the guards arrive. We will meet again, knife.

choices.label: Keep your cult. Pay me and I forget your name.
choices.reply: A practical knife. The Prince approves of that too. Here. And should you ever need a door opened in Cheydinhal, knock twice, then once.

quests.outro: The Thrice-Turned Knife lost its High Blade on a frozen shrine, and Drevis Hlaren climbed into her place over the bodies I left him. At the shrine, Boethiah left a gift in the snow for the knife that turned on its own hand.

quests.title: Mother Mudmouth
quests.offer: You look like you're waiting for someone.
quests.pitch: My hatchling, Little-Reed. He went upriver to Drowned Rest to sell eels and did not come back. The people there smile too much. Do you know what a smile is in the swamp? It is a mouth that has not decided yet.
quests.desc: Seeks-the-Shallows, an Argonian ferrywoman in Leyawiin, asked me to find her son Little-Reed, who vanished in the stilt-village of Drowned Rest.

objectives.text: Travel to Drowned Rest
Watch Drowned Rest after dark
objectives.journal: At midnight the villagers carried a bound stranger down to the water, singing all the way. They were not friendly anymore when they saw me.

objectives.text: Fight the singers of Drowned Rest
Follow the drag-marks to Mudmouth Pool
Kill Mother Mudmouth before she feeds again
objectives.journal: Mother Mudmouth went under for the last time. Little-Reed was tied to a cypress root above the pool, alive, and very angry. I sent him home.

objectives.text: Return to Seeks-the-Shallows in Leyawiin
objectives.topic: Little-Reed is home. The village was feeding travelers to the thing in the pool.
objectives.reply: I know. I have known for six years. They let my boat pass because I paid them in eels and silence. This time they took the wrong child. Mine. You may think less of me. I do too.

choices.label: You should tell the Leyawiin guard everything.
choices.reply: Then I will. The water will be cleaner, and my boat will be emptier. Fair trade.

choices.label: It's over. Keep your secret.
choices.reply: Kind. Or cruel. Hard to tell in the swamp. Take this. It was my mother's, and I do not deserve it today.

quests.outro: Mother Mudmouth is dead, the singers of Drowned Rest are scattered, and Little-Reed is home in Leyawiin. His mother's silence cost more travelers than I like to think about.

quests.title: The Frost-Oath
quests.offer: A song about something that bites back?
quests.pitch: Skeldhaugr. A Nord barrow east of Bruma, older than the city. Hroald Frost-Oath is buried there with a sword called Rimeoath, and the old skalds say he swore to hold something in the ice until the mountains fall. A sword like that deserves to hang in a mead-hall, not rot. Fetch it, and I will put your name in the second verse.
quests.desc: Hrefna Cold-Harp, a skald in Bruma, wants the sword Rimeoath from the Nord barrow of Skeldhaugr for her song.

objectives.text: Find Skeldhaugr Barrow east of Bruma
Fight through the barrow's draugr
Defeat Hroald Frost-Oath
Take Rimeoath from Hroald's throne
Stop Ymmrok before he reaches Bruma
objectives.journal: The giant Ymmrok had been frozen under the Giant's Stair since before Bruma had walls. Hroald's oath was the ice. I broke it, and then I had to break him.

objectives.text: Return to Hrefna Cold-Harp in Bruma
objectives.topic: The sword was holding a frost giant in the ice. Did you know?
objectives.reply: I... knew the verse. Every skald knows it. I thought it was a metaphor. All right, I hoped it wasn't. A saga needs a monster, and Bruma had run out. You must admit it ends well.

choices.label: Your song nearly buried Bruma. The sword goes back to the barrow.
choices.reply: Fine. Fine! Put it back with the old jarl. I'll write it as a tragedy. They sell better anyway.

choices.label: Then sing it well. Here's your sword.
choices.reply: Oh, I will. You'll be the hero of the second verse, and I'll be modest in the third. Here, your fee, and a skald's thanks.

quests.outro: Hroald Frost-Oath and the giant he kept in the ice are both finished, and Bruma has a new song. Hrefna insists the parts about her are entirely accurate.

quests.title: The Lantern on the Larsius
quests.offer: You look like you've lost something.
quests.pitch: My brother Pellio. Went out after a green lantern on the river two weeks back and never came home. Five people have done the same this season. The priests say a drowned spirit lures them. I say find my brother, dead or alive, and Tullo will forgive your next three debts. Generous, yes?
quests.desc: Tullo Brash, a Bravil moneylender, asked me to follow the green lantern on the Larsius that has led five people, including his brother Pellio, away into the night.

objectives.text: Watch the Larsius from the Bravil docks after dark
Follow the green lantern north to Fort Black Boot
Speak with the lantern-bearer
objectives.topic: Pellio? Your brother thinks you drowned.
objectives.reply: My brother hopes I drowned, before I tell anyone what he does. Every one of those 'lost' souls owed Tullo money they could never pay. I row them out of Bravil before his collectors break their hands. And he's sent the collectors after you, friend. They followed you here.

objectives.text: Drive off Tullo's collectors
Kill Grusk gro-Dular, the Collector
objectives.journal: Grusk had a list in his pocket: Pellio's name, the five 'drowned' debtors, and mine, with a sum beside it. Tullo had never meant for me to come back either.

objectives.text: Return to Tullo Brash in Bravil
objectives.topic: I found your brother.
objectives.reply: Found him? Well? Is he alive? And did you, ah, happen to see Grusk on your way?

choices.label: Pellio drowned. So did Grusk.
choices.reply: Drowned. Both. What a terrible river. Here's your fee. Don't spend it all in one skooma den.

choices.label: He's alive, and I know what you are. Your debtors are free.
choices.reply: You... Keep your voice down! Fine. Fine. The debts are torn up, see? Torn up. Now leave Tullo in peace before the guard hears.

quests.outro: The lantern on the Larsius was no drowned spirit, just a brother ferrying debtors out of Bravil ahead of a moneylender's thugs. Pellio still rows at night, and Tullo has stopped asking about him.

quests.title: The Bone-Merchant
quests.pitch: Master Valcis went down through the old outfall beside the lake nine days ago. He said the catacombs under the city were flooding and some of our burials needed moving. He took a lantern and two shovels. He did not take his lunch, and he never forgets his lunch.
quests.desc: Pia Lucanus, apprentice to the Imperial City undertaker Orrin Valcis, asked me to find her master, who went into the catacombs under the city nine days ago.

objectives.text: Find the old sewer outfall beside Lake Rumare
Clear the skeevers from the outfall tunnel
Search the old catacombs under the city
Stop Orrin Valcis in the deepest ossuary
objectives.journal: Orrin Valcis had not been lost. He had been working. Half the paupers he buried for the city were sold to necromancers instead, and he kept the best ones for himself.

objectives.text: Return to Pia Lucanus
objectives.topic: I found your master.
objectives.reply: And? Your face says it before you do. Give me the book. I can read it myself.

objectives.text: Help Pia decide what happens to the shop
objectives.topic: What will you do now?
objectives.reply: Every name in here was someone's grandmother. I could take this to the watch and close the shop forever. Or I could quietly dig them all up, one by one, and bury them properly myself.

choices.label: Take it to the watch.
choices.reply: Then the Imperial City learns its undertaker was a ghoul, and I learn to be something else. Thank you. I mean it.

choices.label: Bury them properly. Quietly.
choices.reply: Then I have a great deal of digging to do. Come by the shop when you want something done right. It will be done right now.

quests.outro: Orrin Valcis, the Imperial City's undertaker, had been selling the dead he was paid to bury. He will not sell any more, and his apprentice is putting things right.

quests.title: The Last Bearer

find.text: Seven headstones in a row on a windy hillside, each for a famous duelist, each dated a few years after the last. The newest is blank except for a scratched line: 'Sir Aemon carried it east, to the white stones of Wendir. Gods help him.'

quests.desc: On a Colovian hillside I found seven duelists' graves, each bearer of the same nameless sword. The latest, Sir Aemon Thrale, carried it east to the Ayleid ruin of Wendir.

objectives.text: Find Sir Aemon Thrale at Wendir
Destroy the hollow shades that follow the sword
Defeat Sir Aemon Thrale and take the black sword
objectives.journal: Sir Aemon thanked me as he fell. The black sword was in my hand before I remember picking it up.

objectives.text: Bury Sir Aemon beside the other six bearers
objectives.journal: I dug the eighth grave and left the headstone blank. The sword said nothing the whole time. I did not care for its silence.

quests.outro: I ended the last bearer of a sword that wears out its owners, and now it is mine. Someday someone may find an eighth headstone on that hill. I mean to make them wait a long time.

quests.title: The Saint's Watchman

find.text: A totem of three bull skulls bound to an oak post. Fresh letters in old Cyrodilic are cut beneath them: 'Son of the Bull, keep the Saint's sleep.' Hoofprints, large ones, lead into the trees. So do boot prints, many of them.

quests.desc: In the Great Forest I found a bull-skull totem with an old Alessian prayer carved on it, and hoofprints followed by a hunting party's boots.

objectives.text: Follow the hoofprints into Bull's Hollow
Stand with Oxhorn against the baron's beaters
Kill Baron Quintus Ardo
objectives.journal: Baron Ardo wanted a minotaur head for his hall in Skingrad. He died certain he was the one doing the hunting.

objectives.text: Keep the night watch at the Saint's cairn with Oxhorn
objectives.journal: Oxhorn told me the cairn belongs to a priestess of Alessia's time, and that his line has kept her grave for a hundred generations. He did not say what happens if she wakes. I did not ask.

quests.outro: Baron Ardo's hunt is over and the minotaur called Oxhorn still keeps his vigil in the Great Forest. He gave me a shield before I left, and said a watchman should not travel unguarded.

quests.title: Forty Drakes
quests.pitch: My mother-in-law's ashes, sera. We carried her urn all the way from Morrowind when we settled here. Two nights ago someone broke the shrine and took her. The guard says bandits. The neighbors say a woman in black has been buying old bones at Fort Scinia, east of the city. Please. She was difficult, but she was ours.
quests.desc: Feldsa Sadrathi, a Dunmer of Cheydinhal, asked me to recover the stolen ash-urn of her family's ancestor, Grandmother Ilmyna.

objectives.text: Ask Feldsa's son Ervyn about the night of the theft
objectives.topic: Where were you the night the shrine was robbed?
objectives.reply: At the tavern! All night. Mostly. Look, nobody liked Grandmother, all right? Even when she was alive she corrected my posture. Now she does it from a jar. Check Fort Scinia, if you must.

objectives.text: Go to Fort Scinia, east of Cheydinhal
Get past the bone-buyer's guards
Stop Calvia Rennus, the Ash-Reader
Recover the Sadrathi ash-urn
objectives.journal: The ghost of Grandmother Ilmyna says her own grandson sold her urn for forty drakes. She seems more offended by the price than by the theft.

objectives.text: Confront Ervyn Sadrathi
objectives.topic: Your grandmother says you sold her for forty drakes.
objectives.reply: She TOLD you? Of course she did. She never stops. Please, don't tell Mother. I'll light her candles every day. I'll even sit up straight.

choices.label: Tell your mother yourself, or I will.
choices.reply: Fine. Fine! But when Grandmother starts on about it, I'm sending her to haunt you.

choices.label: Your secret's safe. Your grandmother is punishment enough.
choices.reply: That's... true, actually. Thank you. Here, it's what's left of the forty drakes. Well, of the ten I didn't drink.

objectives.text: Return the urn to Feldsa Sadrathi
objectives.topic: Grandmother Ilmyna is home.
objectives.reply: Thank the Three and every saint. The house feels like a house again. ...She is already complaining about the dust on the shrine, isn't she? Yes. She is home.

quests.outro: Grandmother Ilmyna Sadrathi is back on her family's shrine in Cheydinhal, telling everyone exactly what she thinks of them. Her grandson now sits up very straight.
